exampleAnswers.title: Calculating a Minor in a NxN Matrix

question.text: What is the minor of $x_{12}$ in $ X= \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 3 & 3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & 1 & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 4 & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}? $
question.explanation:
To get the minor of $x_{12}$, we remove the $1$st row and $2$nd column:

\[ X= \begin{bmatrix} {\color{gray}\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{0} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ 3 & {\color{gray}\ast} & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & {\color{gray}\ast} & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & {\color{gray}\ast} & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \]

So, the minor is

\[ M_{12}= \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 11 & 7 \\ \sqrt{2} & -8 & 8 \\ -6 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}. \]

question.explanation:
First, to get the minor of $g_{42}$, we remove the $4$th row and $2$nd column:

\[ G= \begin{bmatrix} 8 & {\color{gray}\ast} & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & {\color{gray}\ast} & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & {\color{gray}\ast} & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ {\color{gray}\ast} & \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}\sqrt{5}} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} \\ 11& {\color{gray}\ast} & 0 & -9 & 11 \end{bmatrix} \]

So, the minor is

\[ M_{42}= \left| \begin{array}{cccc} 8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11 \end{array} \right|. \]

Now, the cofactor of $g_{42}$ is

\begin{align*} C_{42} &= (-1)^{4+2} M_{42} \\[5pt] &= M_{42} \\[5pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{cccc} 8 & 2 & \sqrt{3} & -2 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{7} & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 11 & 0 & -9 & 11 \end{array} \right|. \end{align*}

First, to get the minor of $d_{51}$, we remove the $5$th row and $1$st column:

\[ D= \begin{bmatrix} \color{gray}\ast & -8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ \color{gray}\ast & 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ \color{gray}\ast & 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ \color{gray}\ast & 0 & 6 & 8& 3\\ \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{\color{gray}11} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} & {\color{gray}\ast} \end{bmatrix} \]

So, the minor is

\[ M_{51}= \left| \begin{array}{cccc} -8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8& 3 \end{array} \right|. \]

Now, the cofactor of $d_{51}$ is

\begin{align*} C_{51} &= (-1)^{5+1} M_{51} \\[5pt] &= M_{51} \\[5pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{cccc} -8 & 2 & 0 & 1 \\ 5 & 0 & 7 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 6 & -4 \\ 0 & 6 & 8& 3 \end{array} \right|. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Calculating the Determinant of a NxN Matrix Using Cofactor Expansion

question.text: Calculate the determinant of the matrix $ S = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 0 & 2 & 2 \end{bmatrix}. $
question.explanation:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

\begin{align*} \det(S) &= s_{11}C_{11} + s_{12}C_{12} + s_{13}C_{13} + s_{14}C_{14} \\[3pt] &= 0 \cdot C_{11} + 2 \cdot C_{12} + 0 \cdot C_{13} + 0 \cdot C_{14} \\[3pt] &= 2C_{12} \\[5pt] & = \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cccc} \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}2 & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ 1 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & \color{lightgray}\ast & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 2 & 2 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 2 (-1)^{1+2} \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -5 & 4 \\ 4 & 2 & 2 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= -2 \left( 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} -5 & 4 \\ 2 & 2 \end{vmatrix} - 0 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 1& 4 \\ 4 & 2 \end{vmatrix} +0 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 1 & -5 \\ 4 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\right) \\[5pt] &= -2 \left((-5 \cdot 2 - 4 \cdot 2)-0+0\right) \\[5pt] &= -2 \cdot (-18) \\[5pt] &= 36 \end{align*}

question.text: Calculate the determinant of the matrix $ W = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1& 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 1 & -2 \end{bmatrix}. $
question.explanation:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

\begin{align*} \det(W) &= w_{11}C_{11} + w_{12}C_{12} + w_{13}C_{13} + w_{14}C_{14} \\[3pt] &= 1 \cdot C_{11} + 0 \cdot C_{12} + 5 \cdot C_{13} + 0 \cdot C_{14} \\[3pt] &= C_{11} + 5C_{13} \\[5pt] & = \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{1} \cdot \begin{vmatrix} \color{lightgray}1 & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ \color{lightgray}\ast & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \color{lightgray}\ast& 3 & 0 & 4 \\ \color{lightgray}\ast & 0 & 1 & -2 \end{vmatrix}+\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{5} \cdot \begin{vmatrix} \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}5 & \color{lightgray}\ast\\ 2 & 0 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & \color{lightgray}\ast& -2 \end{vmatrix} \\[7pt] &= 1 \cdot (-1)^{1+1} \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 &1 & -2 \end{array} \right| + 5 \cdot (-1)^{1+3} \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -2 \end{array} \right| \\[7pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 &1 & -2 \end{array} \right| + 5 \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 2 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 3 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -2 \end{array} \right| \\[7pt] &= 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 0 & 4 \\ 1 & -2 \end{array} \right| - 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 \end{array} \right|+ 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{array} \right| +5 \left( 2 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 \end{array} \right| - 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} -1 & 4 \\ 8 & -2 \end{array} \right|+ 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} -1 & 3 \\ 8 & 0 \end{array} \right| \right)\\[7pt] &= 10 (3\cdot(-2)-4\cdot 0)\\[5pt] &= 10\cdot (-6)\\[5pt] &=-60 \end{align*}

question.text: Calculate the determinant of the matrix $ A = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 8 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix} $
question.explanation:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

\begin{align*} \det(A) &= a_{11}C_{11} + a_{12}C_{12} + a_{13}C_{13} + a_{14}C_{14} \\[3pt] &= 0 \cdot C_{11} + 8 \cdot C_{12} + 0 \cdot C_{13} + 0 \cdot C_{14} \\[3pt] &= 8C_{12} \\[5pt] & = \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{8} \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cccc} \color{lightgray}\ast &\color{lightgray}{8} & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ -1 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & \color{lightgray}\ast & -1 & 2 \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= 8(-1)^{1+2} \left|\begin{array}{ccc} -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 6 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 \end{array}\right| \\[5pt] &= -8\left( (-1) \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 6 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 \end{array} \right| - 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{array} \right| + 0\cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 6 \\ 1 & -1 \end{array} \right| \right) \\[5pt] &= 8(6\cdot 2 - (-1) \cdot 2) - 0 +0 \\[5pt] &= 8\cdot14 \\[5pt] &= 112 \end{align*}

question.text: Calculate the determinant of the matrix $ W = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & 6 \end{bmatrix}. $
question.explanation:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

\begin{align*} \det(W) &= w_{11}C_{11} + w_{12}C_{12} + w_{13}C_{13} + w_{14}C_{14} \\[3pt] &= 0 \cdot C_{11} + (-1) \cdot C_{12} + 0 \cdot C_{13} + 2 \cdot C_{14} \\[3pt] &= -C_{12} + 2C_{14} \\[5pt] & = \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{-1} \cdot \begin{vmatrix} \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}-1 & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ 0 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & \color{lightgray}\ast & 3 & 6 \end{vmatrix} +\bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{2} \cdot \begin{vmatrix} \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast& \color{lightgray}2\\ 0 & 5 & 0 & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ 0 & 4 & 3 & \color{lightgray}\ast \end{vmatrix} \\[7pt] &= -1 \cdot (-1)^{1+2} \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \end{array} \right| + 2 \cdot (-1)^{4+1} \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 \end{array} \right| \\[7pt] &= \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 6 \end{array} \right| -2 \left| \begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 4 & 3 \end{array} \right| \\[7pt] &= 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 6 \end{array} \right| - 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 \end{array} \right|+ 1 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{array} \right| -2 \left( 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 \end{array} \right| - 5 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 \end{array} \right|+ 0 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 \end{array} \right| \right)\\[7pt] &= 9-2\cdot(-5)\cdot9\\[5pt] &=9+90\\[5pt] &=99 \end{align*}

question.text: Calculate the determinant of the matrix $ T = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & 0 & -10 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & -5 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & -25 \end{bmatrix} $
question.explanation:
We use the cofactor expansion along the first row:

\begin{align*} \det(T) &= t_{11}C_{11} + t_{12}C_{12} + t_{13}C_{13} + t_{14}C_{14} \\[3pt] &= 0 \cdot C_{11} + 0 \cdot C_{12} + 0 \cdot C_{13} -10 \cdot C_{14} \\[3pt] &= -10C_{14} \\[5pt] & = \bbox[lightgray, 2pt]{-10} \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cccc} \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast & \color{lightgray}\ast &\color{lightgray}{-10} \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ 1 & 3 & 2 & \color{lightgray}\ast \\ 1 & 2 & 3 & \color{lightgray}\ast \end{array} \right| \\[5pt] &= -10(-1)^{1+4} \left|\begin{array}{ccc} 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 1 & 3 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{array}\right| \\[5pt] &= 10\left( 0\cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 3 & 2 \\ 2 & 3 \end{array} \right| - 4 \cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{array} \right| + 0\cdot \left| \begin{array}{cc} 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 2 \end{array} \right| \right) \\[5pt] &= 10(0-4(1\cdot 3 -1 \cdot 2) +0) \\[5pt] &= 10\cdot(-4) \\[5pt] &= -40 \end{align*}
